title: Physics playground
summary: A 57-body scene: a box pyramid, a pinned bridge, a rope and a wrecking ball. Scene and game code are Dewy, on the bundled physics library.
controls: Drag a body with the mouse. Right-click adds a box; B or middle-click adds a ball; R resets.

title: Dunes
summary: A desert walk with terrain, animated cloth, sand and beam shaders, and sound. The game code and its shaders are Dewy.
controls: WASD or arrows to walk, Space to jump (hold to glide), Q/E or right-drag to turn the camera.

title: Forest
summary: Rolling 3D terrain with 600 instanced trees, a moving beacon, shadows, fog and bloom. Terrain, placement, camera and drawing are Dewy.
controls: Drag to orbit, wheel to zoom, Space toggles the automatic orbit, R resets.

title: Pattern field
summary: A reaction–diffusion simulation built from matrix slices and element-wise arithmetic.
controls: Drag to paint. Sliders set the feed and removal rates; Space pauses, R seeds again.

title: Rollback lab
summary: Two copies of one game over a simulated network: prediction, rewinding and replay with ordinary Dewy value copies.
controls: Sliders set latency, jitter and packet loss. P pauses, R resets.

title: Pendulum
summary: A pendulum with ranged sliders for gravity, length, release angle and damping, and units in its labels.
controls: Drag the sliders. Space pauses, R releases the pendulum again.

title: Charts
summary: Projectile paths with equal axis scales, annotations, dashed lines, grouped bars and a sampled wave.
controls: A still chart page; nothing to control.

title: Camera roll
summary: A rolling 3D camera with labels projected from world positions and cursor-ray picking.
controls: Move the pointer: the orange marker stays under it. The slider rolls the camera; P rotates automatically.

title: Paddle
summary: The smallest game here: 20 lines of game code on a separate, tested model.
controls: Move the pointer to keep the ball in play.

title: Counting words
summary: A dictionary whose lookups are proven present, so there is no KeyError to handle.
source:
text = "the cat sat on the mat and the dog sat too"

let counts:dict<string int> = []
loop word in text.split(" ") {
    if word not in? counts counts[word] = 0
    counts[word] += 1      # proven present: no KeyError
}

loop [word n] in counts if n >? 1 printl"{word} × {n}"
printl"owls: {counts.get("owl") ?? 0}"

title: Units and dimensions
summary: Quantities carry their dimension in the type and print in a fitting unit.
source:
from units import m, km, kg

# A unit is written against its number; dimensions are checked at compile time.
let g = 9.81m/s^2
let mass = 1200kg
let height = 30m
printl"Lifting {mass} by {height} stores {mass * g * height}"

let speed = 25m/s
printl"{speed} is {speed as km/hour}"
printl"A 400m lap takes {400m / speed}"
printl"Exact scales: {3km =? 3000m} {300ms =? 3s/10}"
# 3m + 2s would not compile: a length and a time cannot be added.
stdout:
Lifting 1200kg by 30m stores 353160J
25m/s is 90km/hour
A 400m lap takes 16s
Exact scales: true true

title: Exact numbers
summary: `int` grows as needed, decimals and fractions are exact, and fixed-width integers never overflow silently.
source:
# `int` grows as needed; decimal literals are exact.
let big = 2^200
printl"2^200 = {big}"
printl"0.1 + 0.2 = {0.1 + 0.2}  (equal to 0.3: {0.1 + 0.2 =? 0.3})"

let fact = 1
loop k in 1..30 { fact *= k }
printl"30! = {fact}"

let harmonic = 0/1
loop k in 1..10 { harmonic += 1/k }
printl"1 + 1/2 + … + 1/10 = {harmonic}"

# Fixed-width integers never overflow silently: the compiler must prove the
# result fits, or the type must ask for wrapping.
let counter:uint8<overflow='wrap'> = 250
counter += 10
printl"wrapping uint8: 250 + 10 = {counter}"

title: Dates and time zones
summary: Instants, calendar dates and zoned times, with literals checked while compiling.
source:
# Time needs no import. Literals are checked while compiling.
let launch = instant"2026-10-24T12:00:00Z"
printl"launch + 90 minutes: {launch + 90minute}"

let d = date"2027-01-31"
printl"{d} is a {d.weekday_name}; the next day is {d + 1day}"
printl"one month later, clamped: {d.add(1month overflow='clamp')}"
printl"days until the holiday: {(date"2026-12-25" - date"2026-10-24") / 1day}"

# A calendar week and 168 hours differ across a daylight-saving change.
const meet = zoned"2026-10-26T09:00[America/New_York]"
printl"next week:       {meet + 1week}"
printl"168 hours later: {meet + 168hour}"
stdout:
launch + 90 minutes: 2026-10-24T13:30:00Z
2027-01-31 is a Sunday; the next day is 2027-02-01
one month later, clamped: 2027-02-28
days until the holiday: 62
next week:       2026-11-02T09:00:00-05:00[America/New_York]
168 hours later: 2026-11-02T08:00:00-05:00[America/New_York]
